output.brief: The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14, the March OS patch, the auth-token change, or bots. It was caused by a new vendor rule (AUTO-LIB-17) in Corvane's 3 March rule-pack update. The rule blocks password logins from the app's networking library (nettle-http) when there is no edge session cookie. Evidence: the first blocks were at 10:41 UTC, about three minutes after the pack went live at 10:38. Every app version fails equally, at about 88%, whatever the OS or patch level. All the added failures are HTTP 403 rejections on password submissions. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. The roughly 41,300 blocked installs are mostly genuine customers: 92% had a successful login in the prior 90 days. Credential stuffing is not the explanation. The week's call rise coincides with fee notices, so I can only link it loosely to the login drop. Next step: ask Corvane to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep rate limits, lockout and other rules on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Don't roll back 6.14, don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Confidence is high, though I have not seen Corvane's own account of the rule.
